The sector's flat aggregate masks a bifurcated tape: Indonesian names are outperforming US peers, yet the NORMAL signal argues against chasing broad beta. Rotate into high-momentum insurers and niche lenders, and trim laggards like BTPS if they fail to hold gains.

Nickel and downstream processing names (AADI) ride the EV battery supply chain reshoring wave, with Indonesia's ore export ban cementing local value-add as a durable growth driver.

E-commerce and quick-commerce penetration in tier-2/3 cities is reshaping FMCG go-to-market, giving agile local players a structural cost and speed advantage over legacy incumbents.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in FMCG small/mid caps with confirmed volume breakouts (MSJA, FOLK, KING) as domestic demand holds firm despite US softness; rotate out of laggards lacking earnings catalysts. Target names with strong rural distribution and digital channel growth, as sector consolidation and premiumization sustain momentum through 2H25.

sectors.name: Logistics

Consolidation in the domestic trucking and shipping sub-segments is accelerating, favoring operators with scale and route density (TRUK, SAFE) over fragmented peers.
sectors.ai: Logistics momentum is broad and export-driven, not a one-off. Buy SAFE and TRUK on continued rate normalization and volume recovery; add SHIP for dry-bulk upside. Trim PPGL and TAXI into strength as domestic demand lags. Watch XPO for US freight inflection as leading indicator for Indonesian trade flows. Position size 3-5% each, stop-loss 8% below entry.
